en: Though you are at the point of death.
‘Seizing your elder sister,
I struck your whole village,’ you say,
And again you speak grandly.
‘I made your sister my wife in the wilderness,’ you say,
If I shoot a lot,
‘Smashing your father, Khan Janaaly,
I seized her by force,’ you say.
Is your great Manas here?
You speak without restraint.
Is your great Manas here?
Let me make you lose your composure;
Let me cool, old man,
That far-reaching bluster of yours.
Kokcholok beneath you,
Let me seize it now.
This rumbling old man's
Two testicles, cutting off both,
Let me make him a eunuch.
If you violated my sister,
Old man, let me take my revenge on you this way!
Old man, let me see your might.
Having a halter put upon its neck,
You ask for what you lost;
You keep saying, ‘Zhelmayyan.’
Old man, whom are you mocking?
Are the guardian Kyrgyz here?
Old man, these words of yours are bad words.
Whom are you mocking?
A sharp-tongued woman like you from ancient days!
If your Kyrgyz make you herd camels,
They are your subjects left by Khan Manas.
Old man, Kokcholok, which you will not give if asked,
Let me take it by force.
Your Khan Manas has died;
Let me exact my long-standing vengeance from you.
Let me press down upon your head,
Let me scatter all four kinds of your livestock.
Seizing your mares,
You're gone somewhere.
If you come close, I will strike and scatter your brains,
I will bring out your far-hidden spite.
Let me make you mourn
Your giant, Leopard Manas.
Then let me find for you
A camel such as your Zhelmayyan.
Let me put an end to
Those far-fetched arguments of yours.
Let me seize by force
A beast such as Kokcholok beneath you.
Let me put an end, old man,
To that far-reaching pride of yours.
Wretched old man, you will come to no good!
You will not give up your bluster!
‘I forced your sister,’ you say.
Even as you die, old man,
You will not give up your fury.
Old man, let me split your gallbladder now;
Let me see your vengeance!”
So saying, Semetey
Took the battle-axe in his hand,
Struck Aktulpar once,
Took his sword and drew himself up smartly,
Then lunged toward Bakay,
Making a sudden move.
Then Bakay said this:
“Let me turn my courser's head.
Stand there before me; do not run away.
My child, I will make your mother my wife!
Saddle-sore from herding camels,
I have a beast such as Kokcholok.
Let God strike me forty times outright;
Even if cut into eighty pieces,
My child, I have strength enough for you!
If you ask about my circumstances,
My child, alas, I herd camels.
If God strikes me four times,
My child, I will not spare you.
An inheritance entrusted by my lord,
I have beasts called camels.
Let him strike me ten times at once;
Scoundrel, I have strength enough for you.
Alas, Kokcholok beneath me,
You met it when it had grown thin.
Khan Bakay, who laid waste to this world,
You met him when he had grown old.
This river valley of Talas,
My foal, you met me when it had become my road.
Parted from my tiger,
You met me when I was disgraced.
The marten-fur cap upon my head,
You met me when it had become grass.
My calamities, above my head,
You met me when they had grown many.
My courser saddle-sore, poor creature,
You met it when it had grown thin.
My steel gone, myself dying,
You met me when I had grown old.
My foal who would take Kokcholok,
Stand there before me; do not hurry.
If you are a man, you wretch,
Stand firm; do not run away.
The green river valley of Kapchygay
Was a road I roamed.
Boys such as you,
Eight thousand of them, smashing them,
This was the hand that took them!”
“Manas, Manas!” he shouted;
God now struck the old man.
Striking Kokcholok once,
Frowning in fury,
Bakay came onto the ridge.
His fury grew;
Without sparing his own life,
Bakay saw a birch.
Leopard Bakay, your khan elder,
Had a short-tailed beast beneath him.
Even if sixty Bakays died,
He had the strength of a thousand men.
Bakay pulled the birch, wrenching it over;
The birch, roots and all,
He tore out and overturned,
And made it into a club.
Kokcholok beneath him,
Lashing right and left with his whip,
Spurring on either side:
“My child, if you are strong, stand without haste.
Stand before me; do not run away.
If you stand without fleeing, you are a hero,
A valiant one with strength.
If you stand without fleeing, my foal,
Let me see your strength;
Let me split your head into eighty pieces!
Let me pour out your blood by the leather flaskful;
Let me tear your ribs apart!
My brother-in-law, let me catch you,
Drive you toward your sister,
And finish you in disgrace!
Kara-Shaar and Kambyl,
This is the brother-in-law who besieged them.
Making the camels crack and crash,
This is the hand that beat them.
Havoc upon Kakanchy,
This is Bakay himself who brought it.
From many places, much booty,
This is Bakay who took it.
I took Beijing, let alone mere land,
Raiding farther beyond,
My child, I raided Afghanistan, let alone you.
Your sister in her old age,
My child, you have come to see her.
Your appointed death has come, at your brother-in-law's hands;
My child, you have come to die.
My child, Judgment's narrow road,
My foal, you have come to see it.
Ah, my child, I welcomed you as a guest,
But you have come to hell!”
So Bakay shouted,
Taking the great club in his hand.
Now, as he sought his opportunity,
Now, as he came to strike,
Unable to stand Bakay's heat,
Unable to lie in his cold,
His lower ribs trembling then,
The orphan left by Manas,
His living heart trembled.
Seeing it, his heart was shaken.
Your elder Bakay, the heroic sultan,
Appeared like Ala-Too.
If you saw his figure, Khan Bakay
Thundered like Ala-Too.
The boy who stood watching,
His whole body shuddered.
The boy could not stand it;
His heart was sorely shaken.
Bakay, standing there watching,
Then appeared like a dragon.
The boy could not stand it;
Darting away on Aktulpar,
Semetey shifted his position
And fled in a flash.
‘This powerful Bakay is no good,’ he thought.
‘If I stand my ground, Khan Bakay
Will not spare me with his club,’ he thought.
Then the boy, frightened, darted away;
Your orphan made his escape,
Flashing away on Aktulpar.
Then, shouting “Wretch!” in fury,
Unable to strike Semetey,
Bakay returned to his place, muttering.
The boy had not a fly's strength left.
Fleeing out onto a ridge,
Semetey turned and stood;
Khan Bakay then
He deceived with cries of “Dear brother-in-law.”
“You were a thoroughbred that would never grow thin;
Brother-in-law, you have wasted away.
You were khan to the people of the whole world;
Brother-in-law, you have grown old.
When Khan Manas died, all died;
Their chief, old Bakay, died;
You have fallen into misery.
You did not remain alive; you died.
Brother-in-law, you have seen the face of Judgment.
Brother-in-law, by asking for your Kokcholok,
What wish would I fulfill?
Or my sister who has grown old,
If I took her from you,
Where would I take her?
Herding camels in the wilderness,
Brother-in-law, you have become a quarrelsome man.
When a guest comes, you beat him;
Brother-in-law, you have become rude.
Judgment's narrow road,
Brother-in-law, you have seen it.
When your precious Manas died,
This very year you died.
I journeyed from Chambyl;
Sparing no horse, I traveled far.
My khan brother-in-law who has grown old,
I came to ask after his welfare.
Your Khan Manas has died;
Brother-in-law, I came to pay my respects.
Your famed land of Talas,
Does it remain safe and sound,
Brother-in-law, your small Kyrgyz people?”
Hearing this news,
Bakay now said:
“My child, the people are well, the khan is well;
All the multitude are well.
Tamarisk-covered Keng-Kol is safe;
The small Kyrgyz people are safe.
Making my living by herding camels,
I, your noble brother-in-law, am well.
The horse's mouth is weak,
You ride like an animal.
My child, your spearhead is an armful;
You carry wood unlike the rest.
‘Precious gems come from stone,’ they would say.
‘Wisdom comes from the young,’ they would say.
My child, have you come from Bukhara?
My child, have you heard news from Bukhara?
Alty-Shaar, Margilan,
Below them the khan of Kokand,
Broad-naped Bukhara,
Samarkand beside it—
These were cities standing side by side.
They had messengers;
Caravans used to come;
News used to be heard.
Have you come from the direction of Bukhara?
My child, have you heard news from Bukhara?
When Leopard Manas died,
When the people gathered and buried him,
Kanykey was left in mourning;
Semetey was left an orphan.
